body:
# Independent audit: logarithmic boundary cuts and positive polyhedral parameters

Source read in full: `candidate c3d41384eb67bd52`, Sections 1–6. Verdict: **PASS**, conditional on its stated attained GLOBAL minimum and the separately established enlarged-class attainment. The proof uses no old energy-gradient alignment. Section 4 below gives a simpler exact combined-normalization proof of preservation of the proper improvement.

## 1. Finite majorants and the global-minimum qualification

The sampled-majorant construction is valid. At an actual fiber-interior proper mark, choose a finite supergradient g of the fiberwise concave restriction. The finite array phi_z=max_(K_z)(L-g.X) is sampled-concave: combine actual maximizing points along an anchored relation, use compatibility and joint concavity, and maximize at the target. At the source its value is the supporting affine value. The finite concave base roof therefore has a finite supporting affine plane there, yielding A_p>=L on S with equality at the mark.

This correctly avoids presuming a finite full-space supergradient for an arbitrary real-base extension: 1+sqrt(z) at a boundary base shows why that presumption would fail. The A_p need dominate L only on the sampled set. Each A_p is nonnegative on C by affinity and C=conv(S); their minimum T is concave. The interpolation of T and L remains concave even if T<L at unsampled points.

If T>L on positive mixed volume, write U=T/L-1>=0 on fiber interiors. The exact change of logarithmic mean is M^(-1) integral log(1+tU). Truncating U at a finite bound gives a positive lower bound c t for small t; this does not require a finite derivative. At all proper marks U=0. On fixed small neighborhoods U<c/4, so the normalized parameter strictly decreases there by order t. Outside those neighborhoods the old strict gap persists because the buffers converge uniformly. A remaining equal-value atomic maximum is removed by the actual hinge theorem. This verifies the strict two-stage contradiction.

Equality almost everywhere gives equality throughout each fiber interior by continuity of the concave restrictions. At fiber boundaries E=0, so replacement by T preserves every sampled buffer and its objective; normalization ignores those null sets. The resulting pair is still a GLOBAL minimum. This last statement would not follow merely from local minimality in a topology that distinguishes distant unsampled extensions or replacements. The source explicitly assumes a global minimum, as required.

## 2. The first cut and its logarithmic gain

After replacement, L=min_j A_j is bounded continuous and nonnegative, positive on every sampled fiber interior. If L(v)=0 at a sampled point, choose an active plane A with A(v)=0. Its continuous coefficient is nonzero: otherwise it would vanish on that entire sampled fiber, contradicting interior positivity. Its zero trace has zero d-volume. A cone from v to an interior ball gives positive removed volume for every sufficiently small positive level t. All fibers remain positive for small t because there are only finitely many of them and A is positive at each centroid.

The actual cuts K_z(t)=K_z intersect {A>=t} preserve all anchored inclusions. Canonicalization leaves these integer fibers unchanged. If R_t is the removed mixed set and a_t its mass, then 0<a_t->0 and L<t on R_t, up to immaterial closed level boundaries. Hence

    I_R(t):=integral_(R_t) log L <=a_t log t.           (1)

The source's exact scalar renormalization follows since integral_S log L=0. Integrability of log L also gives

    h_t=a_t|log t|<=-I_R(t)->0,
    h_t/a_t=|log t|->infinity.                         (2)

The logarithm is integrable for the finite-plane representative: on each positive convex fiber every nonnegative affine plane that is positive in the interior has an integrable logarithm, and the negative logarithm of a finite minimum is bounded by the sum of the individual negative parts plus a constant.

Changing the mixed zeroth, first, and second moments by removal of mass a_t from a fixed bounded family changes the within-fiber covariance by O(a_t). Uniform positive fiber volumes and a positive covariance eigenvalue make the resulting norm comparison uniform over all continuous normals. The total mass factor has the same order. Inclusion monotonicity of ordinary energy applies pointwise at every retained mark. Thus the first buffer decrease claimed in the source is valid, without a two-sided energy expansion.

## 3. Uniform proper-strip loss and uniform hinge first variations

The uniform proper-strip argument is particularly useful because it avoids any bound on the integer tilt. At a mark in a fixed interior neighborhood of an old proper maximizing point, consider an old cap of mass <=Q+o(1), and normalize its continuous normal to Euclidean length one. If its own threshold lies s above the lower support of K_p, lowering the entire ambient threshold by s captures the whole own fiber. The actual whole-own-fiber lemma gives total mass at least b_base(p), whereas the all-fiber upper section-area bound permits an increase of at most C s. The fixed positive base gap therefore forces a uniform lower bound on s. A threshold below the source also remains a uniform distance below the upper support since the source neighborhood lies in an interior core.

Sections staying between these two support margins have uniformly positive (d-1)-area. Increasing the threshold by a small length q therefore removes at least c q of OWN volume. This holds at nonsmooth sections, and d=1 uses section measure one. Caps approximating the old infimum to o(h_t) suffice. If the actual buffer decrease is larger than the small guaranteed decrease, use just the first small strip. No upper bound on the energy loss is needed.

The hinge rates in the source may be normalized at the cut family. Their costs converge to positive old costs, so all rates stay bounded and converge. For a positive convex body B and a bounded erosion radius, the inner parallel volume loss is the integral of the surface areas of the inner parallel bodies. As K_z(t) converges to fixed positive K_z and the duration tends to zero, all these inner parallel bodies converge to K_z uniformly over that duration. Surface-area continuity therefore gives the claimed uniform first variations. This argument permits the duration s_t to be comparable to a_t; no comparison between s_t and the geometric height t is required.

Writing m for the number of old compressed atomic caps, the total first loss is m and each selected cap's first loss is at least one. Its mass after the first cut is <=Q. If the hinge duration is s=C a_t, then

    captured_final - beta M_final
        <=beta a_t-s(1-beta m)+o(s).                  (3)

Choose a fixed C with C(1-beta m)>beta, with positive room. Since beta m<1, every old atomic covering cap then has final normalized mass strictly below the original beta. This is a uniform actual estimate, not a derivative taken at the old body while ignoring the first cut.

## 4. Exact combined normalization removes the intermediate growth issue

Let B_t denote the mixed set additionally removed by the hinge, disjoint from R_t, and put D_t=mu(B_t). Uniform bounded hinge rates and surface areas give D_t=O(s_t)=O(a_t). Let

    M_f=M-a_t-D_t.

Keeping the same raw finite-plane L, the final parameter after BOTH sequential logarithmic renormalizations is exactly L_f=c_f L, where

    log c_f=[integral_(R_t) log L
                         +integral_(B_t) log L]/M_f.  (4)

To verify this algebraically, the first log scale is I_R/(M-a_t). In the second removed set, log(c_t L)=log L+log c_t. Adding the second scale (I_B+D_t log c_t)/M_f to log c_t yields (I_R+I_B)/M_f.

Let H=max(0,log max_C L), a finite fixed constant. Equations (1) and (4) imply

    log c_f <=[-h_t+H D_t]/M_f
             <=[-h_t+O(a_t)]/M_f.                    (5)

Other zero faces create no difficulty: they only make the second removed logarithmic integral more negative. Absolute continuity of the integral of |log L| also gives c_f->1, independently of which small hinge-removal sets occur.

The final bodies are nested inside the old ones. Their energy is no greater at retained points. Their total removed mass is O(a_t), so the covariance-norm ratio and the mass normalization contribute at most exp[O(a_t)]. Consequently, at EVERY retained point and for EVERY nonzero continuous normal,

    epsilon f_f(w) G_f(u) / [epsilon f(w) G(u)]
        <= exp[-h_t/(N M)+O(a_t)]
        <= 1-c h_t                                   (6)

for some fixed c>0 and all sufficiently small t, whenever the old denominator is positive. At old fiber-boundary points the new buffer is also zero, so the corresponding weak comparison is immediate. The constants are for the fixed positive epsilon and fixed old family, not uniform as epsilon tends to zero.

Thus after BOTH changes the physical buffer is globally smaller than the OLD buffer. The Section 3 proper-strip argument applies directly to old near-minimizing caps and gives final raw depth <=Q-c' h_t throughout the retained proper neighborhoods. Division by M_f differs from division by M by O(a_t), so the proper normalized maxima lie strictly below beta. At proper points outside those neighborhoods and at old nondeepest bases, nesting and (6) retain the fixed old gap without needing any intermediate depth-continuation estimate. Equation (3) handles every old atomic base. This covers every possible new maximum.

If there are no atomic bases, D_t=0 and the same proof omits the hinge step. If there are atomic bases, the order-h_t proper improvement dominates their order-a_t cleanup cost. All cap orientations and all supporting statuses are retained throughout.

## 5. Audited conclusion and remaining scope

The final normalized buffered maximum is strictly below beta, contradicting the asserted global minimum. Therefore the finite-plane representative cannot have a sampled zero. A zero anywhere in canonical C would force a zero on some sampled fiber because each plane is affine and nonnegative and C=conv(S). The representative is strictly positive on compact C.

This proves the stated positive-polyhedral representative conclusion under enlarged-class attainment and the existing atomic-cover prerequisites. It does not prove a Gamma payment, equate parameter and physical transport measures, or restore the old projective-energy centroid alignment. The logarithmic boundary mechanism is an actual nested-body variation with a quantitative strict surplus, not a formal KKT argument.
